newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia minister sees labour laws by Mar.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia minister sees labour laws by Mar.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Thursday he expected the country's new industrial relations laws to be operating by March 1 next year.

"Hopefully the legislation will be through parliament by October-November. What that means is that the new systems will be in place early in the New Year and operating by February 1 or March 1 -- something of that order," Reith told a Working Women's Service forum.
Reith said debate on the new Industrial Relations Bill would resume next week in the Senate with a more detailed debate the following week.
"I'm very confident that the bill will be through the Senate and the legislation will start next year," Reith told a press conference after the meeting.
"We have political support in the Senate and we are in the process of negotiations (with the Democrats) about amendments," he said.
The bill, a centrepiece of the conservative government's legislative programme, is aimed at reducing the influence of the union movement in the wage negotiating process.
The Democrats have already indicated they would pass the legislation with amendments, Reith said.

Reith said meetings with the Democrats were continuing. "We are getting closer on agreement with the Democrats. We've had many meetings and generally speaking, we are reasonably pleased with the progress," he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373 1800
